question: How do controlled social-exposure descriptions and synthetic persona paragraphs change LLM decisions, and what network predictions follow under an explicitly defined simulation policy?
claim_limit: Human-inspired conditional behavioral audit, not a matched replication of F14 or a validation of human adoption probabilities. Novelty is pending focused related-work review.

execution_changes: Separate R2 unspecified/tied/untied to avoid confounding format with relationship information.
One deduplicated P0 control per condition, with 100 samples rather than pseudo-replicating an absent persona.
Add no-information separately from known zero; add k=4..6 for the selected R1 bridge design.
Five samples per P1 prompt; primary behavioral frequency separated from token score; two held-out amounts.
No claim of complete original ERA, B-1, B-2, B-3, E1-E5, or RCA.
provenance.historical_results: Existing 4B pilots motivated this design. They are development evidence, never pooled as new observations. Main item is not held out.

mistral7b_v03.thinking: not applicable unless backend requires a flag

design.P0: one shared no-persona control per R1/no-information prompt
design.R2_relation: Unspecified for the format comparison; explicit tied/untied only in separate k=2 cells.
design.no_info: No information about adoption, not k=0; one per persona/item/wording, shared across R1/R2 comparisons.
design.heldout_scope: Two new data amounts, 20 fixed personas, w1/R1 only. This tests within-S1 item transfer, not new domains or unseen personas.

bridge_support.required: Before any degree-six R1 macro projection

budget.estimation: Sum per-model call count times representative measured per-call time, plus measured loading overhead and 30% planning margin. Record estimate separately from actual costs.
budget.power: No claim of power from these counts alone. Effects with wide intervals are inconclusive; no unplanned optional stopping.

generation.context: Fresh one-message context per decision; no conversation history, external tools, RAG, or memories. Pretraining knowledge cannot be removed.
generation.ordering: Run one model at a time for memory. Within each approved module/model preserve shuffled manifest order; never select conditions by interim answers.
generation.retry: No retry for an invalid semantic response. Transport errors retained; pause after three consecutive errors and resume only missing requests after fixing the cause, recording attempts.

statistics.primary: T=0.7 semantic Yes frequency on a fixed prompt distribution; retain Yes/No/invalid/error/unattempted separately. Equal P1/persona and wording weights.
statistics.secondary: T=1 exact-label first-token score, raw label mass, candidate coverage and strict-format compliance; never combine it with sampling as equivalent Bernoulli observations.
estimands: persona paragraph contrast and its interaction with k
statistics.independent_units: Synthetic persona blocks for P1; the same persona block retained across doses, wording, representation and model. P0 has no persona clusters: independently resample its unique call draws per cell and reuse each draw across contrasts.
statistics.intervals: 2000 paired persona-block bootstrap resamples; wording treated as three fixed conditions, not a sampled universe of language. For P0/P1 differences jointly resample P1 blocks and P0 calls. Macro uses paired network/trial blocks.
statistics.boundary_cases: All-identical draws can collapse a nonparametric interval; show boundary-aware binomial uncertainty conditional on fixed prompts and do not claim zero probability or proven equality. Synthetic persona intervals do not cover real humans.
statistics.primary_test_family: Eight prespecified two-sided contrasts: per model S2_R1, S2_R2_unspecified, Delta_R, and the P1-minus-P0 difference in [P(1)-P(0)] under R1. Holm correction within this family; effect sizes and pointwise 95% CIs also shown. Other metrics exploratory with clearly labeled CIs.
statistics.testing_method: Centered paired cluster-bootstrap test for non-boundary estimable contrasts; no inferential p-value when bootstrap degenerates or statistic is undefined. Record unavailable rather than report artificial p=0.
statistics.rho_guard: Undefined/unstable when abs(P1-P0)<0.02 or its 95% CI includes zero; do not rank mechanisms using that ratio.
statistics.IC_guard: Plug-in beta and S2/S3 only interpreted as independent-adoption diagnostics when P0<1-1e-6 and 0<=beta<=1. Otherwise report non-admissible IC baseline, dose decrements, and constrained-fit residuals without clamping observed data.

models.M_CAT: Independent probability at each measured dose; nonmonotone reference, not a contagion mechanism.

statistics.comparison: Fit trial-level binary sampling by binomial maximum likelihood per model/representation, core doses only and fixed wordings. BIC counts sampling outcomes, not score rows; five-fold persona-grouped CV keeps every row of each person together. Compare constrained candidates to M_CAT and residuals, not merely to each other. Boundary/saturation fits are flagged; don't infer per-person thresholds from five draws or claim compressed human heterogeneity.
statistics.missingness: Report planned-denominator Yes rates with unresolved bounds; no missing=No. Fit valid binary outcomes transparently, with all-invalid-as-Yes/No sensitivity. A mechanism claim must survive both or remain inconclusive. If >1% core replies unresolved, pause inferential claims and diagnose without repairing historical replies.
statistics.robustness: Strict versus punctuation-tolerant readout; each wording separately and leave-one-wording-out; fixed held-out amounts after main analysis frozen. No result-guided paraphrase deletion.

reproducibility: git hash and dirty status plus source snapshots
